# jsonstor-elasticsearch

> Home: [http://jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com)
>
> Version: 0.1.0

### Documents are stored on an Elasticsearch or OpenSearch server.

Overview
---------------------------------------------------------------------

`jsonstor` defines one interface for working with a document store and implements it
  for a variety of database products and file formats. The interface is the same whichever
  adapter is underneath, so the storage a project uses becomes a configuration decision
  rather than a structural one.

This package is one such adapter. Documents are stored on an Elasticsearch or OpenSearch server.

***It carries no database driver.*** The server is reached over HTTP with the runtime's
  own `fetch`, so this package adds nothing to a project beyond `jsonstor` and `jsongin`.

See [`@liquicode/jsonstor`](https://github.com/liquicode/jsonstor) for the interface,
  and [jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com) for the documentation.

Getting Started
---------------------------------------------------------------------

```bash
npm install --save @liquicode/jsonstor-elasticsearch
```

```js
const jsonstor = require( '@liquicode/jsonstor' )();
jsonstor.LoadPlugin( require( '@liquicode/jsonstor-elasticsearch' ) );

let storage = jsonstor.GetStorage( 'jsonstor-elasticsearch', {
	Server: '...',
	Port: 9200,
	Encrypt: false,
	IndexName: '...',
	PrimaryKey: "_id",
	PrimaryKeyMutable: false,
	PayloadField: "jsonstor_document",
	Mappings: [],
	UserName: "",
	Password: "",
} );
```

Versions
---------------------------------------------------------------------

This package answers to more than one name. Pass any of these to `GetStorage()`;
  a name which is not listed is refused.

| Name | Dialect it uses | Measured against |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | its own | 1.3 |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | its own | 7.17 |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch` | `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | - |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7` | `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | - |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v8` | `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | - |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v8.19` | `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | 8.19 |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v9` | `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | - |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v9.5` | `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | 9.5 |
| `jsonstor-opensearch` | `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | - |
| `jsonstor-opensearch-v1` | `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | - |
| `jsonstor-opensearch-v2` | `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | - |
| `jsonstor-opensearch-v2.19` | `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | 2.19 |
| `jsonstor-opensearch-v3` | `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | - |
| `jsonstor-opensearch-v3.8` | `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | 3.8 |

A name with its own dialect was measured against that server version and covers every
  later one up to the next such name. The rest resolve to one of those. The bare name
  follows the newest dialect this package carries, which is what most callers want.

A name whose dialect your server cannot serve is refused on the first operation, naming
  the version you asked for and the one the server needs.

Settings
---------------------------------------------------------------------

| Setting | Required | Default | Description |
|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| `Server` | ***Yes*** | - | The name or address of the Elasticsearch or OpenSearch server. |
| `Port` | No | `9200` | The service port of the server. |
| `Encrypt` | No | `false` | Reach the server over `https` rather than `http`. There is no `TrustServerCertificate` beside it, because this adapter has no driver except the global `fetch`, which offers no supported way to relax certificate verification. |
| `IndexName` | ***Yes*** | - | The index this storage reads and writes. It is the collection: one index holds one collection's documents. |
| `PrimaryKey` | No | `"_id"` | The document field which is the identifier. Its value becomes the Elasticsearch `_id`. `IdField` is the former spelling and still works. |
| `PrimaryKeyMutable` | No | `false` | Allow an update or replacement to change the identifier. When `false`, such an operation is refused. |
| `PayloadField` | No | `"jsonstor_document"` | The field which stores the document. It cannot be empty: Elasticsearch reserves `_id` as a metadata field, so a document carrying this family's default identifier field cannot be stored at the top level. See the notes. |
| `Mappings` | No | `[]` | The payload fields to give an explicit mapping, as `{ Name, Type }` and optionally `NullValue`. Only a mapped field can be searched on the server; everything else is stored, returned, and filtered by `jsongin`. See the notes. |
| `UserName` | No | `""` | The user to connect as. Empty means none, which is what a server with security disabled expects. |
| `Password` | No | `""` | That user's password. Empty means none. |

Peculiarities
---------------------------------------------------------------------

- ***Elasticsearch and OpenSearch are both supported***, as `jsonstor-elasticsearch` and `jsonstor-opensearch`, from Elasticsearch 7.17 and OpenSearch 1.3.
- ***One index is one collection***, named by `IndexName`. `DropStorage` deletes the index.
- ***The document is stored inside `PayloadField`***, and the Elasticsearch `_id` holds the identifier as a string. `PayloadField` cannot be empty, because Elasticsearch reserves `_id`. Every document reads back exactly as written.
- ***Only fields listed in `Mappings` are searched on the server.*** Other fields are stored but not indexed, and a criteria on them is checked only by `jsongin`. With no `Mappings`, a read reads the whole collection for `jsongin` to check, except a search naming one identifier, which reads that document.
  - `Type` is an Elasticsearch field type: `keyword`, `text`, `long`, `integer`, `short`, `byte`, `double`, `float`, `boolean` or `date`.
  - A `text` field is never searched on the server, because its analyzer ignores case.
  - Without `NullValue`, a field holding `null` cannot be told from an absent one on the server, so `$exists` on it is checked by `jsongin`.
- ***`jsongin` always checks the results.*** On mapped fields, equality, the comparisons, `$in`, `$and`, `$or`, `$exists`, `$regex`, `$all` and `$elemMatch` narrow the search. The negations, `$mod`, the bitwise operators, `$size`, `$type` and `$expr` are checked only by `jsongin`.
- Every write refreshes the index, so a read sees a write which came before it.
- ***No driver is installed.*** The adapter uses Node's built-in `fetch`, so it needs Node 18 or later.
- ***An `https` server with a self-signed certificate cannot be reached.*** `fetch` has no option to accept an untrusted certificate.

Storage Interface
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Every adapter implements the same functions, and they are documented once:
  [Storage Interface](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com/#/guides/Storage-Interface.md).

***The operator list is not repeated here.*** A criteria, a projection, and an update are
  the engine's, and the list changes whenever the engine gains an operator - a copy in this
  file could only ever be out of date. See the
  [Operator Reference](https://github.com/liquicode/jsongin/blob/main/docs/guides/Operator-Reference.md).
